title: Trishul pendant: meaning and symbolism in Shiva worship
description: What the trishul stands for in Shiva worship, the common readings of its three prongs, the damru link, and how to choose and wear a trishul pendant.
intro: The trishul is the three-pronged trident carried by Lord Shiva, and as a pendant it is worn as a symbol of devotion to him and, for many, as a sign of protection. Its three points are read in several ways, most often as the three gunas or as creation, preservation and dissolution. If you are thinking of wearing or gifting one, it helps to know these meanings and a few practical things about pendant size and placement.

sections.heading: The trishul in Shiva's iconography
paragraphs: In almost every image of Shiva, the trishul is close by: held in his hand, planted in the ground beside him on Mount Kailash, or standing at the entrance of a Shiva temple. Many temples also have a large trishul on the shikhara or in the courtyard, and devotees tie red threads or bells to it.

The trishul is not only Shiva's. Goddess Durga holds one too, and in the widely told story of her battle with Mahishasura, the gods give her their weapons, with the trishul coming from Shiva. So the symbol is also seen in Devi temples and during Navratri, which is why trishul pendants are worn by devotees of both Shiva and Shakti.

sections.heading: Three prongs, several readings
paragraphs: There is no single official meaning. These are the interpretations you are most likely to hear from priests, elders and devotional books:
list: The three gunas: sattva, rajas and tamas, the qualities that make up all of nature in Hindu philosophy. Shiva holding them is read as mastery over them.
Creation, preservation and dissolution, the three cosmic functions often linked with Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva.
Past, present and future, with Shiva standing beyond time.
The three worlds: earth, the space between, and the heavens.
Body, mind and spirit, a more modern reading popular in yoga circles.

sections.heading: Why a damru is often tied to it
paragraphs: Look closely at many trishul pendants and you will see a tiny hourglass-shaped drum hanging from the shaft. This is the damru, Shiva's drum. In traditional imagery the two often appear together, the trishul as Shiva's weapon and the damru as the sound of creation. A pendant that shows both is simply following the way Shiva's trishul is painted and sculpted in many temples.

Some trishul designs also include a small Om in the centre, a snake curled around the shaft, or a crescent moon. Each detail points to a different part of Shiva's form, so choose the version that feels meaningful to you.

sections.heading: Choosing a trishul pendant
paragraphs: Since the trishul has a strong, pointed outline, size changes the whole effect. A small pendant of around 2 to 3 cm reads as a subtle devotional piece and suits daily wear, even for women. A larger one makes a bolder statement and is popular with men over a kurta.

On a rudraksha chain, the beads add warmth and texture around the sharp metal shape, which is why this pairing is so common. The [trishul rudraksha chain malas at Varaha](/divine) follow this style, with a gold-plated pendant on a bead chain. If you prefer metal only, a silver chain with a trishul works well for office wear. Whatever you pick, check that the points are smoothly finished, since sharp tips can snag on fabric or scratch skin.

sections.heading: Wearing it with care and respect
paragraphs: Most devotees wear the trishul with the prongs pointing up, the way it stands in temples. Wearing it upside down is generally avoided. Many people also prefer not to wear sacred symbols like the trishul as anklets or toe rings, since the feet are traditionally kept away from religious images.

Some families say a trishul should be worn after a small prayer on a Monday, or after offering it at a Shiva temple first. Others just put it on. Practices vary by region and family, and there is no single correct way. If the pendant is plated, take it off before bathing and keep perfume away from it so the finish stays bright.

If you are gifting a trishul pendant, it suits occasions linked with Shiva or the Goddess: Mahashivratri, a Shravan Monday, the start of Navratri, or a trip to a jyotirlinga. It is also a thoughtful gift for someone setting out on a pilgrimage like the Kanwar Yatra. Add a short note about what the symbol means to you, since that personal touch is what most people remember.

faq.q: Can women wear a trishul pendant?
faq.a: Yes. The trishul is linked with both Shiva and Goddess Durga, and many women wear a small trishul pendant.

faq.q: What do the three points of the trishul mean?
faq.a: Common readings include the three gunas, the cycle of creation, preservation and dissolution, and past, present and future.

faq.q: Is it okay to wear a trishul every day?
faq.a: Many people do. Keep it clean, wear it the right way up, and remove it where your family tradition asks you to.
